state.gainInterpretation: Nonnegative pre-truncation marginal coverage, not degradation

configuration.instructions: Choose INCREASE, KEEP or DECREASE for the next search window. Novelty is the fraction of unique offspring partitions absent from the current parent population. Gain = HV(ND(P union Q)) - HV(ND(P)), before truncation, using frozen normalization. Gain is nonnegative marginal coverage, not a degradation rate or the final retained population HV increase. Use state.gainThreshold as the meaningful per-generation window-mean Gain threshold: meanGain <= gainThreshold is low return, even when strictly positive. A positive Gain alone is not sufficient reason to KEEP. A meanGain above the threshold is evidence of meaningful coverage, not proof that the current probability is optimal. Use state.noveltyThreshold to assess novelty. Reference heuristic: low novelty and low return suggests INCREASE; high novelty and low return suggests DECREASE; sustained meaningful return can support KEEP. These are guidance, NOT mandatory mappings; do not change probability merely to avoid KEEP, and do not assume increasing or decreasing probability will improve final HV. Consider the recent windows, previous actions and subsequent observations; distinguish sustained trends from one-window fluctuations. Changes after an action do not establish causality. Only trigger probability changes; internal crossP stays fixed. Do not invent measurements or future outcomes. Return exactly one offered Choice. Confidence is not evidence of improved decomposition quality.
